title: Sequence-quantile KV profiling + publish pipeline for model onboarding and pinning
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Goal: Build a repeatable pipeline that produces sequence-length quantile performance profiles for each model variant and publishes a canonical profile artifact to the model catalog for use by version pinning and routing policies.

Motivation: Current KV cache heuristics rely on coarse average metrics which miss long-tail and quantile behavior for long-context workloads. Teams need per-model, per-variant profiles that describe latency, throughput, and cache warmup characteristics segmented by sequence-length quantiles (0-25%, 25-50%, 50-75%, 75-90%, 90-99%, 99-100%). These profiles will drive:
- deterministic version-pinning policies for long-context customers,
- autoscaling and warmup strategies tuned by quantile, and
- published guidance in the model catalog for recommended pin/evict settings.

Scope:
- Ingest request traces and token-level timing telemetry from serving runtime for a configurable window (default 72h).
- Compute quantile buckets by sequence-length and produce metrics: median latency, p95/p99, average tokens/sec, KV cache hit/warmup curve, and KV retention sensitivity.
- Derive a simple profile schema (JSON) that includes stable signatures for model+variant+quantile to support pinning TTLs and fallback heuristics.
- Add a pipeline job that validates profile stability across two consecutive windows before auto-publishing to model catalog.
- Expose artifacts in Console under the model page and as a machine-readable endpoint for routing service.

Non-Goals: detailed per-customer privacy filtering (we will anonymize sequence lengths and token hashes), full rework of batching strategies (separate OKR), or changing runtime kernel selection heuristics in this ticket.

Deliverables:
- ETL job in telemetry-service that emits quantile profiles (S3 path and model-catalog registration).
- A profile validator job and gating checks for auto-publish.
- Console UI tile and API endpoint that surfaces the latest profile and recommended pin settings.
- Documentation in Confluence: onboarding playbook and interpretation guide.

Success metrics:
- 95% of models in the onboarding queue have a published profile within 7 days of variant availability.
- For customers using quantile-driven pinning, 10-20% reduction in long-tail p99 token latency for sequences > 4k tokens in first 30 days.
- No regression in overall serving throughput on dedicated pools during profiling runs (<3% CPU/GPU overhead).

Links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/model-quantile-profiles
- Telemetry ETL proto: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/732
- Draft console mockups: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/quantile-profiles-ui
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry ETL job produces stable JSON profile for each model variant and stores under s3://redwood-model-profiles/{model}/{variant}/{timestamp}.json
Profile validator verifies stability across two windows and marks profile as 'canonical' before publish
Model catalog API returns profile URL and recommended pin TTL and warmup vector size
Console model page shows quantile breakdown and recommended pin/evict settings
End-to-end test that simulates synthetic long-tail sequences validates that routing service uses profile for pin decision
tasks: Spec: finalize profile schema and version it (schema v1)
Telemetry: add sequence-length tagging and token-timing extraction in runtime traces
ETL: implement quantile aggregation job and storage format
Validator: implement stability checks and auto-publish gating
Model Catalog: add registration endpoint and UI hooks
Console: surface visualizations and interpretation tooltips
Docs: write onboarding playbook and operator runbook
E2E: create tests and synthetic workloads for validation
Rollout: staged rollout to non-prod, then beta customers, then default publish
risks: Telemetry volume causing ETL cost spikes if sampling not applied
Profiles unstable for low-traffic models leading to churn; will add 'min-samples' threshold
Incorrect anonymization could leak sequence-length patterns (mitigate with aggregation and bucketing)
Publishing an incorrect pin recommendation could impact latency for some customers (gating + manual review for first 2 weeks)
notes: Design decision: use quantile buckets rather than fixed length bands to account for different model tokenization/prompting patterns
We will seed the validator with a manual review step for the first 50 models onboarded
Consider follow-up ticket to feed profiles into autoscaler for quantile-aware policies
Related: ENG-4721 and ENG-10456 contain earlier KV characterization work but do not publish canonical quantile profiles
